tldr: Young people choosing a career often struggle to picture what different paths would actually look like years from now. Future Calling pairs an AI career advisor chatbot with a "Future Envisioner" that turns a chosen occupation into illustrated stories of the user's life 1, 5, 10, and 20 years ahead, complete with step-by-step career paths and face-swapped future-self images. The work explores how generative AI can make long-term career options concrete enough to reflect on and compare.

contributions: Future Calling, a GenAI-based system for career exploration that visualizes future career paths for young users through personalized conversation, stories, and images.
A qualitative exploration of how users explore and refine career options through personalized visualizations and contextual storytelling.
Design insights for career planning systems that use AI-generated personas, with recommendations for extending GenAI to other contexts and audiences.
A demonstration of how GenAI tools can be integrated into social systems to support personal development.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Students and new graduates face career decisions involving many variables, such as job desirability, financial rewards, and personal interest, often with limited access to comprehensive career information. Traditional tools like personality assessments and skills inventories offer a brief view based on past data, and newer machine learning and chatbot approaches still fall short of fully customized plans. Crucially, they rarely provide a visualized career trajectory that users can act on.

Large language models can generate tailored guidance, and text-to-image models combined with face-swap tools can create realistic images of a person's future self. Future Calling brings these together to help young people discover possible career directions and see what those futures might look like.

figures.caption: Users chat with the Career Advisor, which builds a user profile; the Future Envisioner then generates images, stories, and career paths for different occupations that users can customize.

sections.heading: Formative Workshops
paragraphs: To understand how people envision their future selves with GenAI, the team ran individual 30-minute workshops with 19 university participants aged 18–23. After a short demonstration of Stable Diffusion WebUI with Faceswaplab, participants generated images of their appearance, lifestyle, and career one year and twenty years ahead while thinking aloud, followed by a reflective interview analyzed through inductive thematic analysis.
bullets: Difficulty envisioning future selves: participants were unsure of long-term goals and found it hard to write detailed prompts — "I don't even know what I want to do next year, let alone in 20 years."
Lack of narrative depth: images felt impersonal, like "subway ads with no purpose or connection to me."
Positive and creative experiences: seeing future selves reduced some participants' anxiety, and some playfully explored unconventional careers such as superheroes or national leaders.

figures.caption: Formative workshop themes: difficulty envisioning future selves and a need for storytelling in GenAI images, alongside reduced anxiety through positivity and imaginative exploration.

sections.heading: System Design
paragraphs: The workshop insights led to three design responses: guided prompt generation, narrative-driven visualizations, and interactive chatbot support. Future Calling is a React web application with a multi-agent design built on GPT-4, DALL-E 3, and the Baidu FaceSwap API. Users upload a photo and basic information, then move between two modules.

The Career Advisor is a GPT-4 chatbot prompted to keep a gentle, encouraging, and professional tone while gradually eliciting the user's interests and experiences, suggesting occupations along the way. It compiles this into a user profile that is refined as the conversation continues, so users do not have to write image prompts themselves.

The Future Envisioner takes an occupation and the current profile and generates three linked elements for four time points — 1, 5, 10, and 20 years: a future story, a career path with actionable advice, and a future image. Images are generated with DALL-E 3 and face-swapped with the user's photo. Users can give feedback to regenerate any image, story, or career path, and return to explore other occupations.

figures.caption: System design: the Career Advisor (conversational AI) concludes a user profile that the Future Envisioner (text-to-image AI) uses to generate images, stories, and career paths, which users can regenerate with new prompts.

sections.heading: User Study
paragraphs: The team conducted a within-group study with 20 participants (10 male, 10 female, aged 18–25) recruited from universities in China: 10 undergraduates, 6 graduate students, and 4 early-career professionals. Participants completed a pre-survey, and about a week later used Future Calling for around 30 minutes while thinking aloud, then completed a post-survey and a semi-structured interview. Surveys measured career maturity and career self-efficacy using established scales, and qualitative data were coded thematically by two researchers.
bullets: Career self-efficacy increased significantly after using Future Calling (paired t-test, d = 0.652, p = .009).
Career maturity showed a marginal, non-significant improvement (d = 0.447, p = .06).

sections.heading: Use Cases
paragraphs: P8, a student with a political science background and an interest in design, used the Career Advisor to discuss how to connect her background with design work and generated four different career futures, including illustrator and fashion designer. She compared them side by side and asked the advisor about balancing realistic expectations with ideals, handling dissatisfaction in a job she might not like, and income differences.

P11, an engineering student, refined two career plans in depth. He edited the generated career paths to add details and correct inaccuracies, requested more detail, incorporated networking advice from the advisor, and regenerated the 10-year image, so that the plan increasingly reflected his own information and goals.

figures.caption: P8's user flow: conversations with the Career Advisor lead to four envisioned careers, which she compares while asking about realistic expectations, potential dissatisfaction, and income differences.
P11's user flow: refining two career pathways by conversing with the advisor, envisioning futures, and editing prompts and career details through iterative regeneration.

sections.heading: Findings
bullets: Organizing career information: participants valued how the advisor synthesized information faster than a search engine, and some discovered careers they had not considered; others found the information too general or easily searchable.

Reflection through iteration: editing generated stories to fit themselves — correcting unrealistic scenes, adding risks such as losing a job, or adding plans like a master's degree — prompted self-reflection; as P3 said, "It's like I'm starting to understand myself."

Achievable, step-by-step futures: pairing future stories with concrete career advice made goals feel achievable, although some felt 20-year visions were too general and unrealistic compared with specific short-term plans.
Storytelling and images: contextual stories made images feel more meaningful and immersive, though some images reinforced stereotypes such as professionals always wearing suits.

Different needs at different stages: participants still exploring asked broad questions and generated several career plans, while those with clear directions asked specific questions and usually generated only one.
Overly positive futures: optimistic scenarios boosted some participants' confidence and motivation but raised doubts for others, who asked for more balanced or even negative scenarios.

figures.caption: Participants' reactions to highly positive 20-year scenarios: some were skeptical, while others felt the content increased motivation and confidence.

sections.heading: Discussion & Limitations
paragraphs: The authors relate the gain in self-efficacy to future self-continuity: vivid, connected depictions of a future self may strengthen the link between present actions and long-term goals. Career maturity, however, depends on external factors like career education and experience, suggesting the system could integrate mentorship and experiential learning. They also propose retrieval-augmented generation to give users with clear goals more specific information, stricter prompting to reduce overly positive outputs, and AI-framed questions that encourage reflection instead of recommending careers outright, while noting privacy concerns around uploading personal data and photos.

GPT-4 often produced general and positive content, and DALL-E 3 images reflected narrow professional stereotypes. Outcomes were measured only immediately after use, and the study focused on young adults. Future work includes deeper and more specific guidance, broader age and cultural groups, more balanced scenarios, and localized job-market data.
